children: What Happened?
A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after investors shifted their focus from what AI technology can do toward concerns over how companies will finance it.

Driven by these escalating AI funding fears and elevated interest rates, CNBC noted that a massive rotation out of the sector erased more than $1 trillion from the world's largest semiconductor and AI-related stocks this week.

Furthermore, CNBC explained that this funding anxiety triggered counterintuitive moves in the broader market, as investors reassessed the impact of high interest rates on corporate debt-servicing capacity and overall economic growth. Because of these rising structural risks, CNBC reported that safe-haven demand temporarily outweighed inflation fears, prompting capital to exit high-growth tech assets and flow into the Treasury market, which ironically pulled the 10-year Treasury yield down toward 5.09 percent.

Ultimately, according to CNBC analysts, this widespread tech sell-off underscores a growing realization on Wall Street that if the capital-intensive AI trade slows due to financing constraints, broader economic growth will likely decelerate as well.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Zooming In On Bandwidth (BAND)

Bandwidth’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 55 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Bandwidth and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 2 days ago when the stock dropped 6.4% on the news that the major indices pulled back as the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a hotter-than-expected September inflation print, pushing Treasury yields higher. The consumer price index rose 3.7% year-over-year in September, topping the 3.6% estimate from economists polled by Dow Jones. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, climbed 2.6% annually against expectations of 2.5%. Following the print, the 10-year Treasury yield climbed over six basis points to 5.278%, while the 30-year yield advanced past 5.59%, per CNBC market data.Rising yields intensify pressure on equity valuations as third-quarter corporate earnings get underway.

In remarks carried by CNBC, Franklin Templeton Institute head investment strategist Jeff Schulze noted that pressure across the long end of the curve acts as a valuation headwind for risk assets.Higher benchmark yields mechanically elevate the discount rate applied to corporate earnings, compressing the multiples investors are willing to pay for equities. When sticky inflation dampens expectations for monetary easing, the repricing falls heaviest on high-multiple growth sectors whose projected cash flows sit furthest in the future.

Bandwidth is up 200% since the beginning of the year, but at $42.70 per share, it is still trading 45.6% below its 52-week high of $78.44 from July 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Bandwidth’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $473.06.
